content: This judgment from the Court of Foggia Third Civil Section addresses the division of jointly owned property between spouses married under community property regime in 1987 who purchased building land jointly in 2003. Following consensual separation approved in 2006, the defendant spouse made exclusive use of the common land, building a craft workshop and conducting blacksmithing activities thereon. The plaintiff requested dissolution of joint ownership and allocation of respective shares. The court held that pursuant to Article 191 of the Italian Civil Code, spouses have the right to dissolve joint ownership following separation. A court-appointed expert prepared a division plan identifying two distinct portions that could be enjoyed and used independently, including for business purposes. The court approved this plan despite the greater size of one portion, as equal value was achieved through the other portion's direct road access and allocation of fence construction costs exclusively to the larger portion's assignee. The allocation of shares was to be made by drawing lots after the judgment became final, as the shares were equal. The court also granted the plaintiff's request for accounting, holding that the defendant who enjoyed exclusive use of common property since separation approval was required to pay compensation equal to half of the perceivable civil fruits for the property. The court-appointed expert quantified this amount at €24,145.46, from which €3,233.30 was deducted as contribution to management costs incurred exclusively by the defendant and €1,364.59 for concession fees still due, resulting in a final amount of €19,547.57 to be paid to the plaintiff plus legal interest from judgment publication. The essentially non-adversarial conduct of the defendant, who joined proceedings late without contesting division or denying exclusive enjoyment, justified compensation of litigation costs. Technical and administrative costs necessary for division were imposed on both spouses equally as costs incurred in the common interest of the parties.
